sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A Florida jury convicted 54-year-old mechanic Dwain Hall of kidnapping and first-degree murder, sentencing him to life in prison. Hall groomed 32-year-old Sonia Exelby online before she travelled from England to Florida in October 2025. Exelby, from Southsea, Hampshire (reported as Portsmouth in The Guardian), had mental illness and sought someone to end her life. Hall drove her from an airport to a rental, stabbed her to death, and buried her. Hall's defence claimed she took her own life.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Prosecutors stated Hall exploited Exelby's vulnerabilities for sadistic gratification. Exelby's family criticised predatory fetish websites, welcomed the verdict, and pledged to fight for mental health awareness in her memory.

gist: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032.
The proposal involves building four new jails and reducing the detainee population to 4,100.
The correction officers' union criticized the plan, while officials defended the approach.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a plan on Friday to close the Rikers Island jail complex by 2032. The proposal includes building four new jails in Brooklyn, the Bronx, Queens and Manhattan, and reducing the detainee population from over 6,500 to 4,100. Previous closure plans faced delays under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration and due to the Covid pandemic. The City Council must approve the updated timeline.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rikers Island has faced severe backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and nine inmate deaths this year. Supporters describe the closure as a generational opportunity to transform detention and improve inmate outcomes. However, the New York City correction officers' union criticized the plan, arguing that an arbitrary cap on jail beds jeopardises public safety by potentially releasing violent felons.

sections.text: On Friday, students and young workers held coordinated rallies in over 20 European countries. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Federal Communications Commission voted to allow state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming technology against contraband cellphones. sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Murray Warren died at the age of 88. Born in London with a club foot, he spent his early years receiving corrective hospital treatment. After studying at London Bible College, he chose to have his leg amputated below the knee at age 22. He was ordained as a Baptist minister in 1963 before retraining as a teacher. He later served as head at Howbridge junior school and Broomfield primary school, eventually tutoring excluded adolescent boys for the Essex education department.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Warren was remembered as an exceptional teacher who used his understanding of children to make punishment unnecessary. His early childhood experiences in hospital provided him with deep insight into human vulnerabilities and motivations. This empathy allowed him to transform the lives of difficult pupils and offer counselling, coaching, and mentoring to people from diverse backgrounds.

sections.text: Three French police officers were convicted of a racist assault on music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in November 2020. sections.text: Animal rescue NGO Luna and Furry Siblings uncovered 15 dumpsites containing about 170 dead pets across the suburbs of Bulacan, near Manila. gist: A doctor who provided expert evidence in the Lucy Letby trial was barred from practice.
Prof Peter Hindmarsh faced safety concerns regarding his advice on insulin for child patients.
The Crown Prosecution Service continued using Hindmarsh as an expert witness despite these restrictions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Prof Peter Hindmarsh, an expert witness in the Lucy Letby trial, was excluded from clinical practice by his employer, University College London hospitals trust, in March 2023. The trust cited safety concerns regarding his advice on insulin. Despite this, Hindmarsh later provided a crucial expert report for a prosecution against Damion and Tamara Thomas. The jury in the Letby trial was not informed of his exclusion, and the Crown Prosecution Service only learned of the General Medical Council investigation into Hindmarsh in November 2025.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case raises significant questions regarding the use of expert witnesses in court. Legal rules require experts to disclose information that could undermine their credibility or impartiality. Hindmarsh’s failure to disclose his regulatory issues until long after writing his report has led to concerns about whether he complied with these disclosure obligations and whether his evidence was appropriately scrutinised.

sections.text: Promoter DF Concerts has not announced dates, acts, or ticket sales for the 2027 TRNSMT festival. Industry professionals report a lack of communication regarding the event, which is described as unusual compared to previous years. The festival previously faced challenges, including the need to discount tickets for the 2026 edition.

sections.text: TRNSMT has served as a significant platform for emerging Scottish bands. Experts suggest that if the festival ceases, it would represent a cultural loss for the local music scene. sections.heading: What happens next

timeline.text: ‘Shakespearean tale of ego, greed and ambition’: the scandalous story of televangelism

gist: Joe Berlinger directs a new Netflix documentary about 1970s and 1980s US televangelism.
The film focuses on the scandals involving Jerry Falwell, Jimmy Swaggart and Jim Bakker.
The movement's growth intertwined with the rise of the American religious right in politics.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Director Joe Berlinger explores the US televangelism boom in the Netflix documentary Primetime Preacher$. The film focuses on three major figures: Jerry Falwell, Jimmy Swaggart and Jim Bakker. It examines the immense wealth and luxury amassed by Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker through their PTL ministry, alongside external attacks from Swaggart and financial improprieties exposed by Falwell. Scandals, including fraud and sexual misconduct by Bakker and Swaggart, brought down ministries and led to prison time for Bakker.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The rise of televangelism mirrored and fueled the growth of the religious right in American politics. Figures like Bakker backed Ronald Reagan, helping shift a movement that once shunned worldly politics into a cornerstone of the Republican coalition.

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.text: Reports indicate that both the FBI and the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) were hacked. CNN reported that the FBI intrusion targeted the National Crime Information Center, marking the agency's second attack in recent months. Meanwhile, NBC and Reuters reported that the USDA breach affected a payments database, which former officials warned might allow access to sensitive research and food safety data. President Donald Trump later confirmed the FBI breach in an interview with Fox News.

sections.text: The breaches follow recent hacks at the FBI and DHS, as well as outages across the FAA and NSA. Former officials warned the USDA intrusion could provide access to sensitive data, including research on animal-borne illnesses. Meanwhile, platforms like Instagram are developing methods to detect and limit the reach of accounts that repeatedly copy content. gist: Manchester United's managerial hiring and firing costs approach £100m since 2013.
The club borrowed £10m shortly after confirming Mauricio Pochettino as head coach.
Michael Carrick was sacked with the club in the relegation zone.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Manchester United appointed Mauricio Pochettino on a two-and-a-half-year deal and will pay £7.5m in compensation to US Soccer. The club borrowed £10m three days later. Michael Carrick was sacked as manager last week after the club entered the relegation zone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The latest compensation package pushes the total spent on hiring and firing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired to £95m, with costs expected to exceed £100m. United's overall revolving credit debt reached £240m, alongside outstanding transfer fees of £417m.

timeline.text: Australia hold on for narrow win against Wales

gist: Australia defeated Wales in a close Nations Championship match in Cardiff.
Wales fought back with tries from Dewi Lake and Blair Murray.
Australia held on despite a late yellow card to secure victory.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Australia edged past Wales in a tight contest at the Principality Stadium. Tries from Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau helped the visitors build a lead. Wales responded through captain Dewi Lake who scored twice, alongside a try from Blair Murray, but Australia ultimately held on for the win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory ended a four-match losing run for Australia and secured the Nations Championship spoils. For Wales, the defeat highlighted missed attacking opportunities after they failed to capitalise on their chances following their previous notable win against New Zealand.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Wales will play Japan at Twickenham on Saturday. Australia are scheduled to face Ireland on Friday.

gist: England beat New Zealand 37-12 in a repeat of last year.
England played with a more fluid and less predictable style.
New Zealand struggled after a long and tiring schedule.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England secured a 37-12 victory over New Zealand in front of 81,953 fans. Unlike last year when they relied heavily on kicking, England played a more fluid passing game and scored tries through clever movement. Ben Earl made 33 carries, while the forward pack and defence dominated the match against a depleted visiting side.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Steve Borthwick's team has experienced many false dawns and fluctuating form over four years. This win suggests England may have developed a more sustainable tactical approach and deeper squad balance to challenge rugby superpowers ahead of next year's World Cup.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: New Zealand will face England again next Saturday at Allianz Stadium in the Nations Championship third-place play-off. Meanwhile, England's next major challenge will be an away match against Ireland in the Six Nations tournament next February.

gist: Max Verstappen and George Russell will start the Las Vegas Grand Prix on the front row.

The rivalry adds competitive interest to the final races of the Formula 1 season.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Max Verstappen and George Russell clashed during final practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Verstappen was warned by stewards for an unpredictable change of direction under braking after overtaking Russell. Russell responded by pushing Verstappen wide, resulting in light contact between the cars.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident has reignited a long-standing rivalry between the two drivers, who have a history of public disputes. With both championships already decided, the personal animosity between the front-row starters provides a focal point for the remaining races of the season.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Verstappen and Russell are set to start the Las Vegas Grand Prix from the front row. The race is expected to be competitive, with the tow effect on the circuit potentially influencing the outcome and the battle for the constructors' championship.

gist: Price defeated Kotaskova to become undisputed champion in Cardiff.
Price won every round on every judge's scorecard.
Rhys Edwards secured a significant win over Lee McGregor.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Price won every round against Kotaskova in front of a sell-out crowd at the Utilita Arena in Cardiff to become undisputed champion. On the undercard, Rhys Edwards defeated Lee McGregor by unanimous decision to claim the WBA Continental featherweight championship, while Alberto Igancio Palmetta defeated Willy Gilheaney.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory places Price into the record books as she achieved something never done before in Welsh boxing. It drew the attention of former Welsh world champions who were in attendance to watch the history.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Talk immediately turned to a potential stadium fight next summer against five-weight world champion Claressa Shields.

timeline.text: Harden passes Bryant for 50-point games

gist: James Harden scored 51 points in a victory against the Indiana Pacers.
Harden surpassed Kobe Bryant for third place in all-time 50-point NBA games.
The 37-year-old recorded his 26th career 50-point performance during the NBA Cup.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: James Harden scored 51 points for the Cleveland Cavaliers in a 128-119 win against the Indiana Pacers. This performance marked his 26th career 50-point game, moving him past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list. Harden, aged 37, also contributed six rebounds and six assists at Rocket Arena.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The achievement places Harden behind only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan in NBA history for 50-point games. Harden described the milestone as humbling and special, noting the difficulty of maintaining such impact in his 18th season.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Cleveland Cavaliers are scheduled to play the Chicago Bulls on Tuesday.

articles.standfirst: Mykhailo Mudryk accuses Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko of lying about the circumstances surrounding the winger's positive drugs test as his dispute with the country's football federation continues.

timeline.text: Shevchenko accuses Mudryk camp of 'baseless slander'
Shevchenko lying about drugs test claims - Mudryk

gist: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's camp of seeking a false scapegoat for a doping test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed test and subsequent 20-month ban.
Shevchenko denied the allegations, defending the association and asking Mudryk to retract his comments.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andriy Shevchenko stated that Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked for a football federation employee to falsely take the blame for Mudryk's positive test for meldonium. Mudryk, suspended from November 2024 to July 2026, blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for the failed test, claiming it happened on international duty and criticizing a lack of support.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shevchenko called the claims baseless slander and defended the professionalism of association staff, while Mudryk argued the handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

fivew: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives of asking an employee to falsely take the blame for a positive drugs test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed drugs test, prompting a public response from Shevchenko.

quotes.text: baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally
Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps
